accepted.s: The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) is primarily concerned with:
accepted.x: The UNCCD is the international treaty dealing with desertification, land degradation and drought.
accepted.tq: Identify the treaty from its exact subject area.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the UNCCD, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in 1994 in Paris.
2. Its secretariat is located in Bonn.
3. India is a party to the Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the UNCCD was adopted in Paris in 1994, its secretariat is in Bonn, and India is a party.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the treaty’s date, headquarters and membership.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The fourteenth session of the Conference of the Parties to the UNCCD was held at:
accepted.x: UNCCD COP14 was held in New Delhi in 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the conference-number, place and year combination.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: At UNCCD COP14, India raised its land-restoration target to:
accepted.x: India raised its land-restoration target to 26 million hectares by 2030 at COP14 in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Separate the target figure from nearby restoration commitments.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Global Land Outlook — UNFCCC flagship publication
World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought — 5 June
accepted.x: COP17 was held at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, in 2026. The Global Land Outlook is a UNCCD flagship publication and the relevant observance is on 17 June.
accepted.tq: Match each institution or observance with its correct place or identity.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding UNCCD-related initiatives:
1. COP17 was held at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, in 2026.
2. India launched its first guide to Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems at COP17.
3. Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems constitute over 10% of India’s area and less than 5% is protected.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The guide was launched by India’s MoEFCC at COP17 in 2026.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of linked facts through a coded combination.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Global Land Outlook is the flagship publication of the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
accepted.x: The Global Land Outlook is the flagship publication of the UNCCD; editions mentioned include 2017 and 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-publication association.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the UNCCD is correct?
o: It is the only Rio convention dealing with land degradation.
It is a legally binding framework dealing with desertification and drought.
It was adopted in 1996 and came into force in 1994.
It is one of the Montreal Protocol’s implementation agencies.
accepted.x: The UNCCD is the only legally binding framework specifically addressing desertification and drought. It was adopted in 1994 and came into force in 1996, and is one of three Rio conventions.
accepted.tq: Find the precise legal status while rejecting reversed dates and absolute claims.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Bonn Challenge envisages restoration of:
o: 150 million hectares by 2020 and 350 million hectares by 2030
21 million hectares by 2020 and 26 million hectares by 2030
350 million hectares by 2020 and 150 million hectares by 2030
150 million hectares by 2030 and 350 million hectares by 2040
accepted.x: The Bonn Challenge targets 150 million hectares by 2020 and 350 million hectares by 2030.
accepted.tq: Compare the two restoration milestones without reversing their sequence.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Bonn Challenge was launched through cooperation between:
accepted.x: The Bonn Challenge was launched by Germany and IUCN in 2011.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership and year.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. India pledged 21 million hectares under the Bonn Challenge at Paris
B. Bonn Challenge was launched
C. New York Declaration on Forests was made
D. UNCCD COP14 was held in New Delhi
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Bonn Challenge in 2011, New York Declaration on Forests in 2014, India’s Paris pledge in 2015, and COP14 in 2019.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the years 2011, 2014, 2015 and 2019.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed on:
accepted.x: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed on 17 June, following a 1994 UNGA decision.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the environmental observance from other internationally known dates.
accepted.sec: UNCCD - objectives, COP14 in India, LDN target year  [other exams]

accepted.s: According to ISFR 2023, which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Total forest and tree cover — 1,12,014 sq km — 3.41%
accepted.x: ISFR 2023 reports forest cover of 7,15,343 sq km, constituting 21.76% of geographical area.
accepted.tq: Match each category with its distinct area and percentage.
accepted.sec: ISFR - forest and tree cover, state-wise change

accepted.s: According to ISFR 2023, the total forest and tree cover of India was:
accepted.x: The combined forest and tree cover was 8,27,356.95 sq km, equal to 25.17% of the geographical area.
accepted.tq: Combine the two components rather than selecting either component alone.
accepted.sec: ISFR - forest and tree cover, state-wise change

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Survey of India:
1. ISFR is published biennially.
2. The Forest Survey of India was established in 1981.
3. Its headquarters is at Dehradun.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: ISFR is a biennial assessment by the Forest Survey of India, established in 1981 and headquartered at Dehradun.
accepted.tq: Verify the periodicity, establishment year and location separately.
accepted.sec: ISFR - forest and tree cover, state-wise change

accepted.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages forest and tree cover of:
o: 33% of geographical area, including 66% in hills
66% of geographical area, including 33% in hills
50% of geographical area, including 75% in hills
21% of geographical area, including 33% in hills
accepted.x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set a goal of 33% forest and tree cover overall and 66% in hill areas.
accepted.tq: Retain the overall target and the special hill-area target as a pair.
accepted.sec: ISFR - forest and tree cover, state-wise change

accepted.s: Which State has the highest forest cover percentage among the following?
accepted.x: Mizoram has the highest forest cover percentage mentioned, at 84.53%; Andhra Pradesh is reported at 18.28%.
accepted.tq: Use the highest-value comparison rather than the state-specific figure.
accepted.sec: ISFR - forest and tree cover, state-wise change

accepted.s: The type of soil erosion involving uniform removal of a thin surface layer by overland flow is called:
accepted.x: Sheet erosion is the uniform removal of a thin surface layer by overland flow.
accepted.tq: Match the process with its defining physical feature.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Rill erosion — small channels cut by running water
Gully erosion — subsurface removal causing sinkholes
Tunnel erosion — deep trenches of the Chambal
Mass erosion — dust storms in the Thar
accepted.x: Rill erosion forms small channels cut by running water. Tunnel erosion involves subsurface removal, gully erosion forms deep trenches, and wind erosion is associated with dust storms.
accepted.tq: Separate similar erosion types by the feature they produce.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: The Chambal ravines are a characteristic example of:
accepted.x: Deep trenches and ravines, including the Chambal ravines, are characteristic of gully erosion.
accepted.tq: Use the well-known geographical example to identify the erosion type.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Deep trenches are associated with gully erosion, not sheet erosion. Sheet erosion is the uniform removal of a thin surface layer.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped feature in an erosion-type matching question.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: Which of the following measures is most directly intended to reduce wind erosion?
accepted.x: Shelterbelts reduce wind speed and help control wind erosion. Strip cropping and check dams are also conservation measures mentioned for other erosion contexts.
accepted.tq: Apply the conservation measure to the relevant erosion agent.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: China’s straw checkerboards are used primarily to:
accepted.x: Straw checkerboards are used to stabilise dunes and control movement of desert sands.
accepted.tq: Identify the purpose of a named environmental technique.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a soil and water conservation method listed for agricultural areas?
accepted.x: Contour farming, terracing and check dams are conservation measures. Unrestricted removal of vegetation accelerates erosion.
accepted.tq: Reject the practice that worsens the environmental problem.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types and conservation methods

accepted.s: The Watershed Development Component of PMKSY follows which approach?
accepted.x: Watershed development under the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY follows the ridge-to-valley approach.
accepted.tq: Recall the direction of watershed treatment.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Soil Health Cards are associated with village-wise soil nutrient mapping.
2. Agroforestry is supported under the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry and PM-RKVY.
3. MGNREGA and participatory forest management can support soil conservation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. These programmes and approaches support soil assessment, agroforestry, and soil and water conservation.

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, drought-induced land degradation, desertification, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion are especially associated with:
o: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts
Uppada and the Krishna delta only
accepted.x: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai are associated with drought-induced degradation, desertification, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion.

accepted.s: Which of the following regional pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Uppada in Kakinada is associated with coastal erosion. Delta areas are associated with salinity and waterlogging.

accepted.s: According to the AP SDG 15-related figures, the percentage of degraded land in Andhra Pradesh is:
accepted.x: About 33.81% of Andhra Pradesh’s land is reported as degraded under the cited SDG 15 figures.

accepted.s: Which State has the lowest percentage of degraded land among the figures mentioned?
accepted.x: Punjab has the lowest cited degraded-land percentage at 3.15%, compared with 33.81% for Andhra Pradesh.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh:
1. Its desertification area increased by 3.45%.
2. Its tree cover was reported as 2.87%.
3. Its forest cover was reported as 18.28%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three figures are reported for Andhra Pradesh: desertification area up 3.45%, tree cover 2.87%, and forest cover 18.28%.
accepted.tq: Test closely related percentages without confusing their denominators or categories.

accepted.s: Fallow land in Andhra Pradesh is reported to be:
o: 21.26 lakh hectares, or 34.65% of the State
34.65 lakh hectares, or 21.26% of the State
3.45 lakh hectares, or 2.87% of the State
18.28 lakh hectares, or 33.81% of the State
accepted.x: Fallow land covers 34.65 lakh hectares, equivalent to 21.26% of Andhra Pradesh, and exceeds the forest area.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the area figure and its percentage.

accepted.s: The Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh is intended to:
o: Replace watershed development with urban planning
Combat desertification and increase green cover
accepted.x: The Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh is intended to combat desertification and raise green cover.
accepted.tq: Infer the programme’s purpose from its environmental objective.

accepted.s: SPSR Nellore has set a target of achieving what level of green cover by 2047?
